dedupe_keys.name: transportation disadvantage index tdi score charlotte north carolina

description: The Transportation Disadvantage Index (TDI) is a screening layer published by the City of Charlotte on its open data hub to support a high-level assessment of the equity impacts of transport plans and projects. Coverage: polygons across Charlotte, North Carolina, scored on race (Black, Indigenous and persons of colour), income, personal vehicle access, people with mobility impairments, the elderly, youth and populations with limited English proficiency. Users can see where transportation-disadvantaged communities may exist and compare neighbouring communities. Format and access: an ArcGIS feature service (TDI_Polys_New) with the usual hub downloads and API. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: the scoring weights and geography unit are not described in the hub summary read; a screening index, not a measure of access. The layer can weight capacity and investment scenarios in network models towards disadvantaged areas, or overlay outage and disruption results. It relates to the Caltrans Transportation Equity Index in the catalogue.
